Semigration

By: Joy Summers | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Are you thinking of leaving the big smoke and emigrating to the Western Cape- beware the winter and the eye watering property prices

Unique Selling Point:
Taking a new trend of middle and upper class migration across the country and giving it shape with facts and figures from those on the front line who are trying to make their decision work, at a unique moment where technology meets good governance in the Cape.

Summary:
South Africans are voting with their feet, 40 000 have ended their tax residency and emigrated. In Gauteng those that can’t leave are ripping up their lives and heading for the Western Cape, where Covid opened their eyes to remote working.

Joburg’s infrastructure is crumbling and will need to be replaced completely within 5 years, but with a R300 billion backlog, where will the money come from. Many are not sticking around to find out - the Cape offers better run municipalities, great scenery and outdoor living....unless of course its winter - and then you might as well be in England.

And the semigrants are not just going to Cape Town. Small towns from Montagu to Plettenburg bay are experiencing a boom. New arrivals to these towns can see the effects of supply and demand as they try to stretch their Joburg rands to buy something equivalent.

Joburg couple Chris and Jesse are two new arrivals to Montagu. He was a DOP in the advertising industry, she worked as an editor and producer for the BBC and ETV. In 2022 they bought a farm 30 kilometres from Montagu high on the escarpment. Jesse has swopped her natty outfits for gumboots - as they build a new business with a new vision, while still trying to hold onto their old lives. They will take us through some of their trials and tribulations as they transition from city slickers to building a dream in a wild and beautiful landscape.


Further information:
Dries Barnard sells farms in the area. He says they sold 17 farms during lockdown and then it just went crazy. People are coming from all over - Gauteng, Europe, KZN after the riots, Cape Town. The property stats for Montagu themselves show massive growth since 2019.

In Cape Town itself Lightstone stats show the median price of a house in Cape Town is up 161.5% over ten years. In Joburg its only up by 56%. And agents say that selling property in Joburg isn’t easy. Tanya Fourie says what they are seeing is unprecedented as buyers are looking at around 40 properties before they buy.

Carte Blanche will do a comparison of what’s on offer for properties between the R1.5 and R5 million rand market. In Swellendam there are hardly any homes left for sale - move here and you will have to build it yourself. But building costs are up around 35% -even a brick in Johannesburg is R2 cheaper than a brick in George.

But the demand is placing huge strain on the Cape government who will need to build a city the size of Bloemfontein just to accommodate their million new residents.

Moving companies like Biddulph’s are seeing it too. Owen Farmery has created graphs for Carte Blanche, to track the increases since 2016 when incoming and outgoing families was more or less similar. Now they see huge increases in emigration and semigration from Gauteng.

And down at Global Paws - one of the top pet moving companies - they are seeing a similar trend.

So the dogs, the cats and even businesses are moving South. Cape Town has attracted more green economy companies than any other city in Africa In Stellenbosch there are coffee shops buzzing with new start- ups.

Perhaps it’s time provinces battle for their citizens rates and taxes. In the battle between Gauteng and the Cape it appears right now - the Cape is surging ahead. Carte Blanche speaks to agents, economists, Lightstone, those that have semigrated, and the politicians to unpack one of the most important trends taking place right now. South Africans that can are voting with their feet.


Extra Budget Items:
possible some extra travel costs because its Cape, Gauteng and small town about an hour and a half from CT.

Semigration FINAL Script 4th August

Masa Voice over One
The rot had set in long before a main street in Joburg imploded.

Substations explode, collapsed roads are hazardous. There can be no water for days.

R300 billion is needed to fix infrastructure, but the city’s finances are precarious.

Fade to black

Masa Link
Johannesburg has literally imploded and as infrastructure crumbles, many residents have lost faith in officials to turn Gauteng around, so they are leaving and taking their money with them

Masa Voice over Two
400 dollar millionaires left South Africa last year- another 500 are expected to emigrate in 2023.

40 000 South Africans have ended their tax residency in the last five years

At Biddulph’s, South Africa’s largest independent moving company, they’re keeping tabs on the containers they ship offshore. Owen Farmery is the managing director.

Owen Farmery
It's probably at the highest levels we have ever seen. And even this year it’s at 2.63 containers so it’s not slowing down
Masa
What does the 2.63 mean?
Owen
So the 2.63 means that there are 2.63 containers for every one coming back and to put it into perspective each container houses between 1 and five families, so you start doing those numbers it's a lot of people leaving

Masa Voice over 3
And cats and dogs are leaving too. At Global Paws, an international pet transport company, staff get anything from 30 to 60 enquiries per day. Director Dean Emin.

Dean Emin
So at the moment we are seeing anything between 80-100 families per month that we are moving internationally. Emigrating, leaving our shores for foreign climes

Masa Voice over 4
But foreign climes are expensive. Semigration to the Western Cape is a cheaper option, and Gauteng residents who can work remotely are fleeing the province and heading south

Dean Emin
More people are coming down than ever before, it seems like they are coming down en masse. We see it in our requests, Gauteng to CT is the movement of choice at the moment, people want to get to the Western Cape

Masa Voice over 5
And that’s where colleague and Cape Town resident, Erin picks up the story

ERIN LINK
There is semigration where you swop one suburban home for another, and then there is semigration where you upend your entire life

Jesse
So when we moved from Joburg we had - two dogs, one kitty and our two chickens. We had to drive them down here, there is no chicken courier service - we did that in one go

Erin Voice over 6
18 months ago, international TV producer Jesse David Preyser and husband Chris, sold up in Joburg and moved to this farm outside Montagu in the little Karoo

Jesse
It's always been our life ethos to have less of a carbon footprint and when covid happened we lost quite a lot of people in my family and my husband's family and it made us think we could wait until we retired or we could live our lives and do it now.

Erin Voice over 7
Chris was part of a heavy metal band and shot adverts for a living. Now the only heavy metal he works with is a jackhammer, and Jesse elegant wardrobe has been replaced by hardy workwear

Erin
Even your clothing is different?
Jesse
I have a closet full of lovely shirts which I wear when I go to town. I am now a person who says I need to get dressed, because I am going to town.

Erin Voice over 8
Her closest town is Montagu, it’s one of several in the Western Cape, that’s seeing an influx of well-heeled newcomers. R600 000 could buy you a respectable property here just four years ago. But demand means the average property price has tripled in just four years.

Dries Barnard is an agent here who specialises in farms

Dries
Before Covid there was still a steady increase in farm sales, but the moment Covid hit it was just an absolute madhouse. Everybody wanted to get out.

Erin Voice over 9
Dries sold 27 farms in two years and recently studied the values of Montagu farms

Dries Barnard
And in my market in Montagu and surrounds, the capital growth is more than 22%
Erin
And what does that look like in hard numbers?
Dries
if you buy now in 5 years’ time you sell for double. Fantastic for the area.

Masa Voice over 9 A
Back in Gauteng, Biddulph's stats show that Gauteng residents are settling in towns from Plettenberg Bay across to Langebaan.

Owen Farmerey
In 2018 we were doing a total volume of all our consignments coming out of Gauteng going to the western Cape and that percentage was sitting at 19%.

Masa Voice over 10
They compiled these graphs at our request.

Owen Farmerey
By the end of 2022 and you can see the way the graph has moved, we ended up on a graph of 30% from Gauteng to the western cape, that is a 58% increase in total movements
Masa
In just five years?
Owen
In just five years!

Tanya Fourie ringing the bell

Masa Voice over 11
Tanya Fourie sells properties in North riding, Gauteng. She says in 17 years she has never seen a market like this. The exodus has meant thousands of homes here, are competing for buyers




Tanya Fourie, Property Practitioner
If you are going to price a property at fair market value, that is what we would normally do, but if you price it at fair market value you are not in the game, and the biggest driving factor no matter what the property has, is price

Masa Voice over 12
In ten years, according to published figures, the median price of a house in Joburg rose by 55.8% compared to Cape Town, where the average price rise is a whopping 161.5 %.

Masa Voice over 13
To illustrate, Tanya gave us a quick comparison

Tanya
So Masa if you are going to buy in Joburg you are going to get much more value for your buck
So just to give you a rough idea this is one of our properties in North riding- it’s a R3.5 million rand property it’s a free standing house, under roof is 672 square metres. and it’s a seven bedroom property.
Masa
So for 3.5 million rand you can get a seven bedroom pretty much mansion
Tanya
100%. So we pulled something similar in the Cape. For R3.495, you are only going to get a 3 bedroom property, one garage 198 square metre property.

Erin Voice over 14
So in the Cape you are paying a premium for clean governance and service delivery. Nationally, Only 38 municipalities out of 257 achieved clean audits in the recent local government audit outcomes. 21 of those were in the Western Cape.

Anton Bredell
People see the WC as a place of opportunities

Erin Voice over 15
Anton Bredell, the Western Cape MEC for infrastructure, environment and planning, is a busy man. New cities will need to be built over the next 9 years

Anton Bredell
850 000 people will move to the City of CAPE TOWN - the population of Bloemfontein is more or less 900 000 - so that is a Mangaung kind of city that the City of Cape Town needs to build within the city. Schools, hospitals, water networks - roads ...it's huge

Erin Voice over 16
His stats show that Stellenbosch, Montagu, Hermanus, George, Mossel Bay, Swartland, Saldana and Paarl will grow at around 4%. For a province short of water, this is a massive challenge

Anton Bredell
We understand that the 125 000 people moving to the Western Cape in 12 months- we need 25 million litres of extra water per day. The year before 108 000 people moved to the Western Cape. That was 2020 - 2021, so in 24 months we need now- forty seven million litres of extra water per day, so it's huge.

Erin Voice over 17
The Western Cape is aiming to create 640 000 jobs to accommodate the influx. Up on the hill in Montagu, Jesse and Chris are creating their own, building an eco-tourism business

Jess
Garlic, goats and goodness, that is what we are aiming for

Erin Voice over 18
But it’s been incredibly tough just to get the basics right, starting with enough water and dry boreholes

Jesse
People come with sticks and you pay them quite a lot of money to pinpoint holes for you. It was 222 metres deep and dry - so I sold my car to pay for that.

Erin Voice over 19
When they did find water it needed to be filtered, and then the pumps didn’t work, when there was loadshedding, so they had to find funds for a solar system.

Jesse
So we were always going off grid that was the long term plan but having no water and no electricity, okay well, we might as well move back to Joburg
ERIN
Every stop on the road there has been a curved ball or an additional expense or a challenge - at what point do you go this was a terrible idea?
Jesse
Uh Every three months - like quarterly - every 3 months our rule is- oh are you freaking out? And the money is going away and we don't know what we're doing? Go stand outside and look how pretty it is. That is the only thing we can do - going outside and look at the view - why am I here? We give it 5 years, and if we are screwed, we sell it.

Erin Voice over 20
But where will Gauteng be five years from here? For now it is still South Africa’s wealthiest province but the Western Cape is catching up.

Masa Voice over
Premier panyaza Lesufi couldn't make our interview on Gauteng's plans, because his team said he was in New Zealand.

Street explosion and aftermath

But he magically appeared when Lillian Ngoyi street exploded in downtown Joburg. And as the Cape plans whole new cities, Gauteng is trying to figure out exactly how an entire Joburg street imploded.

THE END

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Are you thinking of leaving the big smoke and emigrating to the Western Cape- beware the winter and the eye watering property prices
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Taking a new trend of middle and upper class migration across the country and giving it shape with facts and figures from those on the front line who are trying to make their decision work, at a unique moment where technology meets good governance in the Cape.
metadata.Summary: South Africans are voting with their feet, 40 000 have ended their tax residency and emigrated. In Gauteng those that can’t leave are ripping up their lives and heading for the Western Cape, where Covid opened their eyes to remote working. Joburg’s infrastructure is crumbling and will need to be replaced completely within 5 years, but with a R300 billion backlog, where will the money come from. Many are not sticking around to find out - the Cape offers better run municipalities, great scenery and outdoor living....unless of course its winter - and then you might as well be in England. And the semigrants are not just going to Cape Town. Small towns from Montagu to Plettenburg bay are experiencing a boom. New arrivals to these towns can see the effects of supply and demand as they try to stretch their Joburg rands to buy something equivalent. Joburg couple Chris and Jesse are two new arrivals to Montagu. He was a DOP in the advertising industry, she worked as an editor and producer for the BBC and ETV. In 2022 they bought a farm 30 kilometres from Montagu high on the escarpment. Jesse has swopped her natty outfits for gumboots - as they build a new business with a new vision, while still trying to hold onto their old lives. They will take us through some of their trials and tribulations as they transition from city slickers to building a dream in a wild and beautiful landscape.
metadata.Further information: Dries Barnard sells farms in the area. He says they sold 17 farms during lockdown and then it just went crazy. People are coming from all over - Gauteng, Europe, KZN after the riots, Cape Town. The property stats for Montagu themselves show massive growth since 2019. In Cape Town itself Lightstone stats show the median price of a house in Cape Town is up 161.5% over ten years. In Joburg its only up by 56%. And agents say that selling property in Joburg isn’t easy. Tanya Fourie says what they are seeing is unprecedented as buyers are looking at around 40 properties before they buy. Carte Blanche will do a comparison of what’s on offer for properties between the R1.5 and R5 million rand market. In Swellendam there are hardly any homes left for sale - move here and you will have to build it yourself. But building costs are up around 35% -even a brick in Johannesburg is R2 cheaper than a brick in George. But the demand is placing huge strain on the Cape government who will need to build a city the size of Bloemfontein just to accommodate their million new residents. Moving companies like Biddulph’s are seeing it too. Owen Farmery has created graphs for Carte Blanche, to track the increases since 2016 when incoming and outgoing families was more or less similar. Now they see huge increases in emigration and semigration from Gauteng. And down at Global Paws - one of the top pet moving companies - they are seeing a similar trend. So the dogs, the cats and even businesses are moving South. Cape Town has attracted more green economy companies than any other city in Africa In Stellenbosch there are coffee shops buzzing with new start- ups. Perhaps it’s time provinces battle for their citizens rates and taxes. In the battle between Gauteng and the Cape it appears right now - the Cape is surging ahead. Carte Blanche speaks to agents, economists, Lightstone, those that have semigrated, and the politicians to unpack one of the most important trends taking place right now. South Africans that can are voting with their feet.
